text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers.
DER STANDARD

- Leading members of Social Democrat's regional branch in Styria demand Chancellor and party chief Franz Vranitzky should prepare for a new leadership by 1997 after the party suffered heavy losses in Sunday's European parliamentary elections.
- Vienna Social Democrats likely to enter a coalition with conservative People's Party after losing absolute majority in Vienna state elections on Sunday.
- Social Democrats see no need to hurry a decision to liberalise shopping hours after conservative Economics Minister Hannes Farnleitner has asked for comment on new legislation by next week.
- Aluminium maker Amag, about to be privatised, expects operating losses of 150 million schillings this year.
- Exports to other European Union countries went up ten percent as a result of Austria's membership in the EU, overall exports up seven percent in the first half.
DIE PRESSE
- Trade union chief Hans Sallmutter says Franz Vranitzky should not be federal chancellor and Social Democratic party chief at the same time.
- Austria's entry into the EU was the right thing to do, and staying out of the union would have been more expensive, economic expert at Vienna university says.
- Petrol prices raised by 0.20 schillings per litre after oil price hits a new high.
- Unions say they will block Economics Minister Johann Farnleitner's attempts to liberalise shopping hours.
- Austrian firms are losing ground in Hungary and the Czech Republic amid increased competition from French and Italian rivals.
KURIER
- Vienna mayor and Social Democrat leader Michael Haeupl for the first time meets with far-right Freedom Party representatives to discuss cooperation on the regional level.
- Union chief Hans Sallmutter says growing rift between social partners puts increasing strain on centre-left government coalition.
- Austria's top five retail chains control 80 percent of the national market, concentration in the industry is rising across Europe.
- Supermarket chain Meinl expected to report 50 million schilling operating loss this year.
- Rising crude oil prices causes inflation gains across Europe.
- Austria imported more electricity than it exported in the first nine months of 1996.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- German cigarette maker Reemtsma denies it is interested in taking over state-owned Austria Tabak.
